# accmeta

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/giuseppealfonzetti/accmeta/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/giuseppealfonzetti/accmeta/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Penalised estimation of meta-analysis models for diagnostic accuracy, in terms of sensitivity, specificity and prevalence. Three estimators are available: a trivariate linear mixed model
(TLMM) using a within-study normal approximation, the trivariate
generalized linear mixed model (TGLMM), and an iterative bootstrap (IB) that corrects
the bias of the TLMM by simulating from the TGLMM. IB fits come with a
covariance matrix and Wald or basic confidence intervals, built from a simulated
Jacobian of the TGLMM score.

## Installation

You can install the package via 

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pak::pkg_install("giuseppealfonzetti/accmeta")
```

## Example

Setup true parameter value

```{r truepar}
library(accmeta)

th <- c(2.94, -2.2, -0.4, 0.0953, 0.4, -0.5108, 0.3, 0.2, -0.6931)
theta2list(th)
min(eigen(theta2list(th)$SIGMA)$values)

```

Simulate data from true model

```{r data}
set.seed(1)
x <- sim_data(15, th, sample(40:200, 15, TRUE))
head(x)
```

Counts go in through `set_meta_data()`, which checks them and computes the
summaries the models need. 

```{r meta}
d <- set_meta_data(x)
d
```

A continuity correction is needed by the approximate
model whenever a cell is empty. You can use the CC argument:

```{r}
d_cc <- set_meta_data(x, CC = 0.5)
d_cc
```


Now we can fit the models. Note that the TGLMM can be directly fitted on the original data.

```{r fits}
tlmm <- fit_tlmm(d_cc)
tglmm <- fit_tglmm(d)
ib <- fit_ib(d_cc)
ib
```

The IB stops when the Mahalanobis distance of its last step falls below `PRECISION / H`
Monte Carlo variances (`"converged"`), when it stops improving (`"stall"`), when the next
update would leave the box (`"boundary"`) or after `MAX_ITER` iterations (`"maxit"`). These
settings, and the box bounds, are set through `set_ib_control()`.

`coef()` extract estimated parameters:

```{r coef}
coef(tlmm)
coef(tglmm)
coef(ib)

```

All models are estimated, by default, with the recommended Wishart prior. You can change it via

```{r}
tglmm_mle <- fit_tglmm(d, PRIOR = set_prior(DEGREES = 4, SCALE = Inf))
coef(tglmm_mle)
min(eigen(coef(tglmm_mle)$SIGMA)$values)
min(eigen(coef(tglmm)$SIGMA)$values)

```

## Inference for the IB estimate

With `VCOV = TRUE`, `fit_ib()` also computes the Jacobian at the estimate.  `NCORES` spreads both the
simulated fits of each iteration and the Jacobian draws for parallel computations
```{r ib-vcov}
ib <- fit_ib(d_cc, VCOV = TRUE, CONTROL = set_ib_control(NCORES = 4))
```

`update(ib, VCOV = TRUE)` adds the Jacobian to an existing fit, using the fit's `CONTROL`.
`vcov()` and `confint()` work in the working coordinates of the IB, i.e the means, the log
standard deviations and the Fisher-z partial correlations.

```{r ib-ci}
sqrt(diag(vcov(ib)))
confint(ib)
confint(ib, METHOD = "basic")
```

Intervals for the means map to the natural scale; specificity is one minus the inverse logit of
`mu_xi`, so its bounds swap.

```{r ib-natural}
ci <- confint(ib, parm = 1:3)
rbind(
  sensitivity = plogis(ci["mu_eta", ]),
  specificity = unname(1 - plogis(ci["mu_xi", 2:1])),
  prevalence = plogis(ci["mu_gamma", ])
)
```
